newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Nishat Mills seen robust.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Nishat Mills seen robust.

text.p: Pakistan's Nishat Mills is seen robust over the next 12 months on a turnaround in the textile sector after last year's duty cuts on imported polyester fibre, a research report said on Monday.

"Financial year 1996 marked a revival of fortunes for the local textile sector, with Nishat Mills showing a net profit of 135 million rupees, up from only 30 million rupees, the year before," said International Asset Management Company Ltd (IAMC) in its quarterly report.

"Margins recovered on the back of lower raw material costs and firm output prices. Gross and operating margins for Nishat Mills recovered to 15 percent and 10 percent respectively... We expect this recovery to continue in the financial year 1997."
On Monday, Nishat Mills fell 0.50, or 2.17 percent, to 22.50 rupees a share at the Karachi Stock Exchange in a turnover of 3,500 shares.

Nishat Mills is Pakistan's largest textile unit, with 45 million kg of production capacity and more than 100 million dollars in annual export sales. The toal asset base is more than seven billion rupees, and share holders' equity is more than three billion rupees, the report said.
"It is this balance sheet size that makes Nishat Mills practically the only serious consideration in the textile sector in Pakistan for most foreign investors," it said.
The report said a 10 percent duty reduction on imported polyester staple fibre further reduced input costs for spinners of blended yarn.
"Cotton prices have not firmed up, even after the current crop size of 8.5 million bales against initial estimates of 10 million bales or more."
Prospects of further devaluation of the Pakistan rupee should help exporters like Nishat Mills.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan adjusted the rupee downward to 40.2400/40.4412 to the dollar on April 23 from 40.1200/40.3206.
"It really should not come as a surprise that Nishat Mills ... (has) outperformed the market since the fourth quarter of financial year 1996," the report said.
"We expect the textile counter to continue performing strongly over the next 12 months," it added.
